market_mood: Markets bounced into month-end with a record Black Friday retail backdrop and an AI relief rally, while Middle East supply fears (an attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, Iran tensions) keep a floor under oil and jet fuel.
self_check: My high-confidence calls have been badly wrong (14%) while low-confidence ones did best, so I'm avoiding 'high' entirely today; oil and rates themes have been my worst, so I kept energy sizing modest and leaned on consumer and geopolitics, which have worked.

picks.reason: An attack halted part of Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery and Reuters flags a global diesel deficit coming in 2027, which supports refining margins for US refiners.
Record Black Friday and holiday spending data with value-hunting shoppers supports discretionary retailers heading into December.
Iran warning over Gulf naval presence, Turkey ratifying the Mecca defence pact and a hack of the Air Force's Cloud One platform all point to sustained defence and secure-IT spending.
A holder opposing the Advantage Energy sale could trim or delay a deal investors worried was pricey, while firmer oil on supply fears supports cash flow.
A breach of the Air Force's Cloud One platform should drive federal cyber spending.

watchlist_notes.note: Broad rally into month-end (+1.6% on the day) but still down ~6% over the month, so the tone is relief rather than trend.
Tech was the only weak sector last week; the AI bounce after Jensen Huang's return looks fragile.
Dow rose in the post-holiday session, helped by banks, miners and consumer names.
A $799 smart-glasses startup challenges Vision Pro, a reminder of rising competition but not a near-term earnings issue.
No major company news; sentiment tracks the broader AI-spending debate.
Shares lagged a rising market despite Huang's return, showing AI jitters haven't fully cleared.
Strong Black Friday data and record online spending support the retail and AWS story.
Down sharply in the selloff; debate centers on heavy capex versus solid search and cloud results.
Facing Australia's Digital Duty of Care and EU AI rules while exploring Japanese AI data centers.
Jumped ~5% on unconfirmed SpaceX merger chatter, a rumor-driven move that can reverse fast.
Part of a $400m+ muni bond price-fixing settlement, a manageable cost, and it called bitcoin capitulation.
Energy stocks rose with oil's first weekly gain of November on Middle East supply fears.
Gold is steady as risk appetite returns; miners rallied globally.
No major rates news today; month-end flows dominate.

top_buys.pitch: Refinery outages abroad and a looming diesel deficit favor US refiners.
top_buys.why: An attack halted some operations at Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, removing product supply from the market. Reuters separately reports the global diesel market heading into deficit by Q2 2027. Tighter product supply typically widens crack spreads, which is the main profit driver for refiners like Valero. Energy stocks were already firming Friday with oil's first weekly gain of November.
top_buys.risks: If the Jazan outage is brief and oil's supply fear fades, crack spreads could give back gains quickly; refiners are volatile and my energy calls have a poor record.
top_buys.watch: Weekly EIA distillate inventories and any update on Jazan restart timing.

top_buys.pitch: Record holiday spending and value-hunting shoppers favor a discretionary retailer with momentum.
top_buys.why: Adobe data points to record online holiday spending and retailers expect robust demand through Black Friday and beyond. Beauty has been one of the most resilient discretionary categories when shoppers trade down elsewhere. Consumer discretionary was up 3.5% last week, so the tide is with the trade, and my consumer calls have been my best theme lately.
top_buys.risks: Heavy promotions could mean strong sales but weaker margins, and a soft Cyber Monday read would deflate the group.
top_buys.watch: Cyber Monday spending data and Ulta's next quarterly report in early December.

top_buys.pitch: Gulf naval tension and a US Air Force cloud breach keep defense budgets flowing.
top_buys.why: Iran warned over expanding foreign naval presence in the Gulf while South Korea readies a bigger role, and Turkey ratified the Mecca defence pact. Hackers also breached the Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform, which tends to accelerate secure-IT and mission-systems spending. General Dynamics has exposure to both shipbuilding and government technology services, and my geopolitics calls have had the best hit rate.
top_buys.risks: Defense stocks have already run on war headlines, and any Ukraine or Iran de-escalation would take air out of the group.
top_buys.watch: Any US naval deployment news in the Gulf and December defense contract awards.

top_buys.pitch: Deal pushback plus firmer crude is a decent combination for a big low-cost producer.
top_buys.why: A shareholder is voting against the Advantage Energy sale to Canadian Natural, which raises the chance the acquirer avoids overpaying or walks away. Meanwhile oil posted its first weekly gain of November on supply fears tied to the Jazan attack and Iran tensions. CNQ is a lower-volatility way to express a firmer oil tape than small producers.
top_buys.risks: Oil's bounce could fade quickly if OPEC adds barrels or Middle East risk cools; the deal objection may be a minor holder with no influence.
top_buys.watch: The Advantage Energy shareholder vote outcome and next week's crude direction.

top_buys.pitch: A breach of the Air Force's Cloud One platform should drive federal cyber spending.
top_buys.why: Reuters reports hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform. Federal cyber incidents reliably lead to remediation contracts and higher security budgets for government IT contractors. Booz Allen is one of the largest providers of that work and hasn't been obviously connected to the headline yet.
top_buys.risks: Government services stocks have been pressured by budget and efficiency cuts, and the link to any single contract is indirect.
top_buys.watch: Follow-up reporting on the breach scope and any emergency federal cyber funding.

summary.big_story: An attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery and Iran tensions drove oil's first weekly gain of November, even as US stocks rallied on record Black Friday spending.
summary.top_pick: Valero, because refinery outages abroad plus a forecast 2027 diesel deficit point to stronger refining margins that the market hasn't fully priced.
summary.watch: Whether crude holds its gains into next week's OPEC headlines, and Cyber Monday spending data.
